S_nonExistentCatalogBodies.evidence: Per body: horizonsResponseText is the verbatim Horizons sentence; terminatesAfterTdb is the date it names.

T_staleUnanchoredIsANonExistenceSignal.statement: anchorSource stale-unanchored on an NEA-class body is already a non-existence signal. Re-anchoring requires a Horizons state at the 2026-05-01 re-anchor epoch, which an object that has ceased to exist cannot provide, so the re-anchor fails and the body retains its original SBDB epoch.
T_staleUnanchoredIsANonExistenceSignal.whyLikelyAndNotEstablished: The mechanism is inferred from the perfect correlation plus the pipeline design; the ingestion code path itself was not traced.
T_staleUnanchoredIsANonExistenceSignal.boundedness: The set is bounded: an object that impacted BEFORE the re-anchor epoch could not have re-anchored, so no catalog-wide sweep is required to find more.

U_epochAgeControlRetired.statement: The epoch-age control (addition P) is retired as a MEASURED PROPERTY, not an error. Element-epoch age has no variation among NEA-class bodies that still exist: the only NEA-class bodies with an epoch older than 2026-01-01 are exactly the non-existent bodies above, and all 309 sbdb-anchored bodies are 2026-era (at most ~0.2 y older than the 2026-05-01 mass epoch). Epoch age now varies only in the comet band (3D 1832, 323P 2021, 12P 2023).
